label: copy phase: re-fed n when the next output is 0 (late in long sequences)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (100% of mass), almost always when the fed-back input is n (93% of mass; a few on input 0). It is strongest when the original bigram is n followed by 0, so the model is about to output 0 (out_tok=0 holds 72% of mass); the top examples are all "n 0" patterns copied at recall positions 5-7. Magnitude grows with sequence length and recall position: no activity for L<=4 or recall_idx<3, and the rate peaks at t=16 in L=9 sequences. Weaker activations come from input n when the next output is another token (z, n, f), and from input 0 before a second 0. It never fires in the original or delimiter phases, or on the first occurrence of a token. Precision is limited: many short or early n->0 copies stay silent, so the predicate is about 45% precise and 50% recall (67% of mass).
